newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk parliament debate on minister set for May 20.
newsitem.headline: Turk parliament debate on minister set for May 20.

text.p: Turkey's parliament will vote on May 20 on whether to launch an investigation into Interior Minister Meral Aksener over claims she abused her position, an opposition deputy said on Wednesday.

The ballotting will be a fresh test for Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition with conservatives, which has already survived a series of parliamentary challenges since it came to power last June.

Murat Basesgioglu, an MP from the main opposition Motherland Party, said any inquiry would determine if Aksener had acted illegally in the removal of national police chief Alaadin Yuksel in a clandestine, overnight sacking in March.

The government, battered by fierce criticism from the secularist army, has a majority of only a handful of MPs and the loyalty of some backbenchers from the True Path Party coalition partner is questionable.
Basesgioglu told Reuters a vote was also to be held on May 13 on setting up a probe into an armed attack on a private television station and its subsequent closure last week.
Police have arrested five suspects from among up to 60 men involved in Friday's attack on Flash TV's Istanbul studios.

The media linked the attack to a Flash telephone interview with organised crime boss Alaattin Cakici in which he implicated several leading public figures in corruption. Police forced the channel off the air on Saturday.
It was up and running again on Sunday but the television watchdog ordered it closed for two days this week over the Cakici interview.

Organised crime and its links with the state and government have been on the agenda of Turkey's parliament since a crash in November when a top policeman and a wanted gangster were killed in the same car.
A former interior minister resigned after being implicated in the scandal.
